guide_enrichment.narrative:
For us, the case is less about Kansas’ 51-6 opener and more about whether its rebuilt offense showed transferable strengths. Kansas produced 613 yards, while new starting quarterback Isaiah Marshall completed 14 of 19 passes for 246 yards and added 49 on the ground. The offensive line also allowed no sacks and only one tackle for loss. Long Island was a limited first test, but those results offer useful context for an offense replacing nine starters rather than proof that the transition is complete.

What stands out in our numbers is Kansas’ ability to create scoring opportunities against an Arizona State defense that has not graded as consistently at preventing them. Marshall’s mobility and Nik McMillan’s immediate production—six catches for 130 yards in his Kansas debut—give Kansas multiple ways to move the ball. That matters because the market is asking Arizona State to create meaningful separation, while our view is that Kansas has enough offensive functionality to stay within range.

The concern for us is Kansas’ pass defense. Our matchup grades identify Arizona State’s passing game as the clearest place the favorite can outperform our expectation. Kansas does return cornerbacks Jalen Todd and Austin Alexander along with safety Taylor Davis, so there is some continuity in the secondary, but this remains the main challenge to our position.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
We are watching Arizona State’s passing offense against the Kansas secondary. If Arizona State consistently generates efficient gains through the air, it has the clearest path to creating the separation the market expects.

Kansas’ best response is to disrupt those attempts before they develop. The defense recorded 11 tackles for loss and three sacks in the opener, although we are not treating production against Long Island as conclusive. For us, the useful question is whether that pressure carries over well enough to protect the area our numbers identify as Kansas’ biggest vulnerability.

recent_game.fact: Kansas opened the 2026 season with a 51-6 win over Long Island on Sept. 4.
Kansas produced 613 total yards on 76 plays against Long Island, including 277 rushing yards and 336 passing yards.
Kansas held Long Island to 146 total yards, 35 rushing yards on 33 attempts and no touchdowns.
Kansas recorded 11 tackles for loss and three sacks against Long Island.

opponent_notes.fact: Arizona State opened the 2026 season with a 70-7 win over Morgan State.
Arizona State is scheduled to play at Texas A&M on Sept. 12 before facing Kansas on Sept. 19.
Arizona State wide receiver Omarion Miller entered the week with consecutive 100-yard receiving games.

quarterback.fact: Kansas named redshirt sophomore Isaiah Marshall its starting quarterback before the 2026 season, replacing a position primarily held by Jalon Daniels during the previous six seasons.
Marshall completed 14 of 19 passes for 246 yards and two touchdowns and rushed seven times for 49 yards against Long Island.
Backup Cole Ballard completed 4 of 6 passes for 90 yards in the opener and has 535 passing yards and three touchdowns in his Kansas career.

Quarterback Chase Jenkins transferred to Kansas after starting all 12 regular-season games for Rice in 2025, when he passed for 1,025 yards and nine touchdowns and rushed for 531 yards and five touchdowns.

offensive_personnel.fact: Kansas' Game 2 depth chart listed Dylan Edwards or Yasin Willis at starting running back, with Jalen Dupree behind them.
Willis rushed 11 times for 72 yards and two touchdowns against Long Island, while Dupree had nine carries for 35 yards and a touchdown and Edwards had six carries for 32 yards.
Willis transferred from Syracuse, Edwards transferred from Kansas State and Dupree transferred from Colorado State.
Buffalo transfer Nik McMillan caught six passes for 130 yards and a touchdown in his Kansas debut against Long Island, extending his streak to seven consecutive 100-yard receiving games.

Kansas' Game 2 starting offensive line was listed as Calvin Clements at left tackle, Amir Herring at left guard, Kasen Carpenter at center, Tavake Tuikolovatu at right guard and Nick Morrow at right tackle.
Clements and Herring are the two returning starters on Kansas' offensive line; Carpenter transferred from Oklahoma State and Morrow transferred from California.
Kansas lost nine offensive starters from 2025, including quarterback Jalon Daniels, running back Daniel Hishaw Jr., center Bryce Foster, guard Kobe Baynes and tackle Enrique Cruz Jr.

defensive_personnel.fact: Defensive end Leroy Harris III recorded a career-high four tackles for loss against Long Island.
Michigan State transfer David Santiago recorded four tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery against Long Island.
Linebacker Trey Lathan returns after leading Kansas with 86 tackles in 2025; he entered 2026 with 198 career tackles and 17 tackles for loss.
Kansas returns 2025 cornerback starters Jalen Todd and Austin Alexander, who combined for 22 starts last season, along with returning safety Taylor Davis.
Kansas added experienced safeties Corey Gordon and Jaden Harris; Gordon started all 12 games for Louisville in 2025, while Harris previously started 13 games for Miami in 2024.
Kansas returned five defensive starters from 2025: Trey Lathan, Austin Alexander, Taylor Davis, Blake Herold and Jalen Todd.

coaching_changes.fact: Andy Kotelnicki returned to Kansas as associate head coach after spending two seasons at Penn State; he previously coordinated Kansas' offense from 2021 through 2023.
Kansas' 2026 staff lists Jim Zebrowski as passing game coordinator and quarterbacks coach, Matt Lubick as co-offensive coordinator and tight ends coach, and D.K. McDonald as defensive coordinator.

injury_availability.fact: Wide receiver Cam Pickett did not play in Kansas' season opener against Long Island.

offensive_context.fact: Kansas scored five rushing touchdowns against Long Island, with Willis scoring twice and Dupree, Micah Johnson and Donald Collier each scoring once.
Kansas generated six plays of more than 20 yards, including three plays of more than 40 yards, against Long Island.
The Kansas offensive line allowed no sacks and only one tackle for loss against Long Island.
Kansas has allowed 45 sacks since the start of the 2023 season, the second-fewest total in the Big 12 over that span.

defensive_context.fact: Kansas allowed 26.8 points and 387.2 total yards per game in 2025.
Kansas allowed 214.1 passing yards per game in 2025, its lowest season average since 2001.
Kansas averaged 6.3 tackles for loss per game in 2025, ranking fourth in the Big 12.

special_teams.fact: Kansas added kicker Martin Connington from Michigan State, long snapper Rino Monteforte from California and freshman punter Matt Gill for 2026.
Connington made a 32-yard field goal and all six extra-point attempts against Long Island.
Kansas' Game 2 depth chart listed Dylan Edwards as the primary kickoff returner and Tate Nagy as the primary punt returner.

series_context.fact: Arizona State leads the series with Kansas 1-0 after defeating the Jayhawks 35-31 in Tempe in 2024.

other_relevant.fact: Kansas and Arizona State are scheduled to play Sept. 19, 2026 at Wembley Stadium in London in each team's Big 12 opener.
The Kansas-Arizona State game will be the first international game for both programs and the first college football game played at Wembley Stadium.
